title: Shift compatibility of the reduction and total-limit adjunction
statement: Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. For finite-type $k$-schemes $W$ with their small pro-etale sites put $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$, and let $\mathscr S_W$ be the abelian category of strict semilinear systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves, with its ordinary unbounded derived category, derived reduction $\mathcal R_W$ and total-limit functor $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; regard $\mathscr S_W$ as the module category of the ring diagram $((A_n)_W)_n$ on the simultaneous ringed diagram site of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization, def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Equip the reduction functor $\mathcal R_W$ and the total-limit functor $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ with the termwise cochain-shift comparisons, using the functorial total derived limit of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], computed on a K-injective tower resolution; its Roos triangle is in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit], and its shifted-cone model uses the cochain convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The derived adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] has unit $u:P\to\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_WP$ and counit $e_N:\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WN\to N$. For every integer $r$, both $u$ and $e$ commute with the shift comparisons, naturally in $P\in D(\widehat R_W)$ and $N\in D(\mathscr S_W)$, including the signs from the shifted Roos cone. Equivalently, for every coefficient calculus S supplied by [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] together with its coherence data, the stated shift comparisons and unit/counit compatibilities exist.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal V=W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $A=\widehat R_W$ and $B_n=(A_n)_W$. Use the small sequence site $\mathcal T$ of [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], with ring sheaf $B=(B_n)_n$. Projection $\mathcal T\to\mathcal V$ gives a morphism of topoi: inverse image is the constant-system functor (the sheaf condition is levelwise), and its right adjoint is limit. The constant-system functor preserves finite limits, since these are computed levelwise. The compatible quotient maps $A\to B_n$ give a ring map from the constant ring sheaf $A$ to $B$. Denote the resulting morphism of ringed topoi by $p:(\mathcal T,B)\to(\mathcal V,A)$. Its module direct image is $p_*M=\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_nM_n$, and its module pullback is $p^*Q=(Q\otimes_A B_n)_n$, with the actual quotient transitions. The module adjunction is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]: concretely, a compatible family of $B_n$-linear maps $Q\otimes_A B_n\to M_n$ is exactly an $A$-linear map $Q\to\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_nM_n$. These formulas specify the whole system map, including its transition equations.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), projection from the sequence site; sites-modules.tex Tag 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] to $p$. On a flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to P$ it computes $Lp^*P$ by $(Q\otimes_A B_n)_n$. Thus its canonical resolution comparisons identify $Lp^*$ with the actual functor $\mathcal R_W$ in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], including the quotient transitions and induced maps of resolutions. Its integer-shift comparison is the stated termwise one: $Q[r]$ is an allowed shifted representative by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift], and $(Q[r]\otimes_A B_n)^i=Q^{i+r}\otimes_A B_n$ has differential $(-1)^r(d_Q\otimes1)$. Hence the identity on these terms is the comparison $(Q[r]\otimes_A B_n)_n\to(Q\otimes_A B_n)_n[r]$. No tensoring by a non-flat quotient is asserted to preserve arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms; only the K-flat computation is used.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); derived.tex Tag 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact), with the canonical-resolution shift normalization stated in lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift.

proof.text: Factor $p=g a$, where $a:(\mathcal T,B)\to(\mathcal T,A^{\mathrm{const}})$ is the identity-topos ring change and $g:(\mathcal T,A^{\mathrm{const}})\to(\mathcal V,A)$ is projection. Then $a_*=U$ is the exact restriction functor of [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], and $g_*=\lim$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], $Ra_*=D(U)$; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] therefore gives the canonical comparison $Rp_*\cong R\lim\,D(U)=\mathcal L_W$. It preserves the specified shift comparisons, as follows directly from that node's normalization. For K-injective $I$ on $(\mathcal T,B)$ and a K-injective replacement $j:UI\to J$, the comparison is represented by $\lim j$. For shift $r$ use $I[r]$ and $j[r]:U(I[r])=(UI)[r]\to J[r]$, which are permitted by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift]. The two maps are literally equal after $\lim(J[r])=(\lim J)[r]$, since their degree-$i$ component is $\lim j^{i+r}$. This also identifies the shift on $\mathcal L_W$ with that computed on a simultaneous K-injective $A$-tower, rather than a choice of triangles.

Under steps 2 and 3 the canonical adjunction $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$ is precisely $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]: both use the derived adjunction of the same module adjunction in step 1 and its canonical resolution comparisons. In particular its unit has the actual reduction components and its counit is obtained by transposing the actual total-limit projections, with their simultaneous system compatibility. We use this canonical adjunction identification, not an inference from equality of evaluated derived arrows. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift] to the small ringed topoi of step 1. If $\rho_{P,r}:\mathcal R(P[r])\to\mathcal R(P)[r]$ and $\lambda_{N,r}:\mathcal L(N[r])\to\mathcal L(N)[r]$ are the comparisons just identified, the conclusion gives
$$\lambda_{\mathcal RP,r}\,\mathcal L(\rho_{P,r})\,u_{P[r]}=u_P[r],\qquad e_{N[r]}=e_N[r]\,\rho_{\mathcal LN,r}\,\mathcal R(\lambda_{N,r}).$$
These are equations of derived system transformations for every integer $r$, natural in $P,N$. They require neither normalization of $N$ nor derived completeness of $P$.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); derived.tex Tag 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact), using the canonical integer-shift compatibility in the cited DAG theorem.

proof.text: For the cone-model comparison, take a K-injective resolution $U N\to I_\bullet$ in constant-$A$ towers with injective terms, as permitted on the small constant-ring sequence site by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. It computes total limit by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Each transition of an injective tower object $J$ splits: let $T_n(F)$ be $F$ at indices $1,\ldots,n$, with identity transitions there, and zero at larger indices. A map $T_n(F)\to J$ is uniquely a map $F\to J_n$. The inclusion $T_n(F)\hookrightarrow T_{n+1}(F)$ is monic by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. With $F=J_n$, extend the map corresponding to $1_{J_n}$ across this inclusion using [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; its component at $n+1$ is a section of $J_{n+1}\to J_n$. Apply this to $J=I^i$ for each degree $i$. Products of module sheaves exist: form them sectionwise, and glue matching families in each coordinate. Thus [lem-weil-roos-split-comparison] applies and gives the quasi-isomorphism $\eta:\lim I_n\to\operatorname{Cone}(h)[-1]$, $z\mapsto(0,z)$, where $h=1-s$ on $\Pi=\prod_n I_n$. Its formula is natural in strict tower chain maps.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), injective-tower computation; injectives.tex Tag 079P; elementary finite-prefix argument for split transitions; kernel-to-cone comparison supplied by lem-weil-roos-split-comparison.

proof.text:
Each $I_n$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective], so [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective] identifies $\Pi$ with the derived product in the Roos triangle of [def-weil-derived-limit]. In the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], put $C(I)=\operatorname{Cone}(h)[-1]$. Then $C(I)^i=\Pi^{i-1}\oplus\Pi^i$ and $d(y,x)=(-dy-hx,dx)$. For every integer $r$ define
$$\chi_r:C(I[r])\longrightarrow C(I)[r],\qquad (y,x)\longmapsto((-1)^r y,x).$$
This is a chain isomorphism: applying its target differential gives $(-dy-(-1)^r hx,(-1)^r dx)$, which is also $\chi_r$ applied to the source differential $((-1)^{r+1}dy-hx,(-1)^r dx)$. Its inverse has the same formula, and $\chi_r\eta_{I[r]}=\eta_I[r]$ because the first coordinate of $\eta$ is zero. Hence the signed Roos shift comparison agrees with the total-limit shift used in steps 3 and 4. Both cone coordinates are transformed by the same product map on a tower chain map, so $\chi_r$ is natural and the equation descends to the chosen derived model. The signs satisfy the shift-addition rule $(-1)^{r+s}=(-1)^r(-1)^s$, also for negative shifts. Thus the unit and counit equations of step 4 include the shifted-cone signs, without assuming exactness of products of arbitrary sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), derived product and Roos triangle; derived.tex Tag 0BK6 (lemma-product-K-injective). Agent sign calculation in the stated cochain-cone convention.

proof.text: The preceding arguments apply to all the objects in the statement. For $r=0$, all representative comparisons and $\chi_0$ are identity. For $r=1$ and $r=-1$, $\chi_r$ negates the cone's first coordinate, as required by the shift differential; two such shifts negate it twice. For the zero object every displayed morphism is the unique zero morphism. A degree-zero coefficient sheaf and a one-step shift give the termwise reduction map in its shifted degree, with no additional scalar sign; the extra sign is confined to the first cone coordinate. The empty scheme gives zero module categories. No $n=0$ quotient occurs. Naturality follows from the canonical derived comparisons and the explicit natural cone formulas, so these checks impose no additional hypotheses.
